title: Web render finish: board and cover materials read in the page rendering, then deploy on approval

Executed by command; output written to runs/wo-gh-14/test-writer.output.md

Loopback to builder: S10 scope: the diff from setup commit 62f98b3 to HEAD, excluding evidence/ and runs/wo-gh-14/, lists only blender/build_patch_one.py, scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs, src/patch-one-glb.js, src/take-apart-client.js, tests/take-apart.test.js and tests/web-render-finish.test.js. All are allowed. The capture script change only adds a CAPTURE_DIR output selection and a second pass log, which the before/after capture needs. Tests: tests/web-render-finish.test.js changes only its SETUP_COMMIT constant. tests/take-apart.test.js changes SETUP_COMMIT and the scope whitelist, which S10 allows as a re-base, and no assertion changes meaning. Result: the web-render-finish suite runs 16 of 16 passing.; S1/S5 (R5) budget: the GLB is 798,088 bytes (budget 819,200), 4 bytes under the 798,092 baseline. The size is stated in builder.output.md, reproducibility.log and both browser-pass logs (GLB status 200, bytes 798088).; S3 reproducibility: reproducibility.log records two consecutive `blender --background --python blender/build_all.py` runs on Blender 4.5.15. Both give GLB sha256 1b9bab70... and module sha256 3ea15ceb..., and the committed src/patch-one-glb.js equals the export. Build logs 1 and 2 are committed. I did not re-run Blender, so I rely on those logs.; S2/R6 frozen product: frozen-product.log says nodes, meshes, accessors, scenes and the binary payload are byte identical to the setup asset, and only material JSON differs. The Python diff touches only the silicone mapping scale and normal strength, the LED emission strength and the plated-contact color and roughness. No geometry, wordmark or LED position or proportion changes. The product is frozen as S2/R6 require.; R4 client scope: the src/take-apart-client.js diff changes only the exposure, ambient fill, key and rim lights, a generated PMREM environment, and on-load per-material adjustments (envMapIntensity by metalness, the optical lens, a cover grain shader hook). The state-function binding, node binding by name, tour, controls and quality tiers are untouched. The vendored three.js and page chrome and copy are not in the diff, and web-render-finish tests 14 and 15 pass. One point for reviewer-design to weigh: the Optical silicone window is forced to a teal emissive in the client, a real compensation for the ×8 vertical exaggeration but a larger change than a plain intensity tweak.; R7/R8/S7 evidence: evidence/web-render-finish/before/ (taken from an archive of 62f98b3, original client and asset, with source.log hashes) and after/ each hold five beats, a browser-assembled shot, a contact sheet, a bundle-build.log and a browser-pass.log. Both pass logs show console errors 0, page errors 0, scene ready true, GLB fetched with status 200, five named nodes loaded, gauge PASS and asset-failure checks PASS. The bundle build runs `wrangler deploy --dry-run` with exit status 0 and 'No local patches applied'. The worker is served with --no-bundle from the built output, so no evidence step loads the unbundled source. evidence/take-apart/ and the beauty renders under evidence/take-apart-product-model/ are regenerated and show the 798088-byte asset. Note: builder-notes.md says the execution wrapper returned 143 on shutdown after the final captures completed. The logs show a clean pass, so this is a note, not a defect.; S4/S5 visual (spec-side check only; the judgement belongs to reviewer-design): in the after beat-assembled.png the teal LED line is visible on the cover where the before beat showed it gray. The cover shows soft grain and a shaded crown, and the board edge shows warmer pad highlights. Beat files for apart, mid, board and xray all differ in size from the before set, which shows a rendering change. The after cover micrograin is subtle at beat resolution, so reviewer-design should confirm it against the mid and board beats and the contact sheet.; S9/S8 suite: suite.log shows 212 pass and 1 fail (the design v4 S11 test 'when reviewer-design has reviewed, it addresses and clears all four images against design/reference/'), plus the one existing skip. builder-notes.md itemizes that failure by name as pre-existing and resolved on anvil/run-s11-rebaseline (wo-gh-10). It was not absorbed and no other run's evidence was edited. I did not re-run the full suite.; Gap: the spec does not require beauty-render identity to be re-judged by this station, so S6 identity is left to reviewer-design. Deployment and the verdict are outside this station, and the builder output explicitly states no approval or deployment was performed.; src/take-apart-client.js: the changes only touch rendering (a procedural PMREM studio environment, lights, tone mapping exposure, per-material tweaks). They add no network fetches, eval or Function calls, innerHTML, new dependencies or user-input handling.; The onBeforeCompile shader patch for 'Matte off white silicone' is a static string replacement of three.js shader chunks with constant values, so there is no injection surface.; The temporary studio scene's geometries and materials and the PMREM generator are disposed after the environment is generated, so no resource leak.; scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs: the new CAPTURE_DIR env var sets the output directory and does not normalize '..' segments, so a hostile value could write outside evidence/. This is low risk because it is operator-set dev tooling and not reachable from the served app. I suggest constraining it to evidence/.; src/patch-one-glb.js is a data-only module with no executable logic added. Vendored three.js, package manifests and page chrome are unchanged. No secrets or unsafe defaults were introduced.; The review file is written to runs/wo-gh-14/reviewer-security.output.md.; I ran `node --test tests/web-render-finish.test.js` on the final tree. All 16 tests pass (16 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped). Round 1 had 9 pass and 7 fail, and those failures came from the missing builder output. The tests themselves are unchanged in substance.; I ran `npm test`. The result is 212 pass and 1 fail, and the one failure is `not ok 98 - S11: when reviewer-design has reviewed, it addresses and clears all four images against design/reference/`. That is the single pre-existing design v4 S11 failure the work order itemizes. Nothing else fails, and the builder did not absorb the failure or edit evidence to hide it.; The builder edited the tests, within what S10 permits. In `tests/web-render-finish.test.js` the only change is `SETUP_COMMIT` moving from `4de668a` to `62f98b3`. In `tests/take-apart.test.js` the baseline constant moved the same way, and the scope allowlist was re-pointed at the wo-gh-14 paths. S10 allows re-basing a scope or baseline constant 'with its assertions' meaning unchanged'. The allowlist rewrite also removed the old wo-gh-9 and `src/index.js` and `src/page.js` entries, so the assertion is no weaker. The S10 test passes against the new baseline.; The test evidence is real and mapped. The tests map to scenarios S7, S8/R4 and S10 by name. The committed logs are `evidence/web-render-finish/behavior-tests.log`, `suite.log`, `bundle-build.log`, `frozen-product.log` and `reproducibility.log`. Before and after beats and browser pass logs exist under `evidence/web-render-finish/before/` and `after/`.; `reproducibility.log` records two consecutive full Blender 4.5.15 builds with the same GLB SHA256 (`1b9bab70…`) and the same module SHA256. It states the committed `src/patch-one-glb.js` equals the export byte for byte. The GLB is 798,088 bytes against the 819,200 budget, down from 798,092, and the size is stated.; I did not open the before and after PNGs. Whether both finish problems are closed in the page rendering is reviewer-design's call and is not covered by these tests.; Minor: the capture script `scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs` gained a `CAPTURE_DIR` option and writes the pass log twice. S10 allows this because the before and after capture requires it, and the default output paths are unchanged.; Scope (S10): the diff from setup commit 62f98b3 to HEAD touches only blender/build_patch_one.py, src/patch-one-glb.js, src/take-apart-client.js, scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs, tests/take-apart.test.js, tests/web-render-finish.test.js, evidence/ and runs/wo-gh-14/. There are no changes to vendored three.js, page chrome, the model or interaction code, or other runs' evidence. brain/decisions does not exist in this repo, so I checked against the spec and brain/project.md only.; Both sides of the problem are handled where the spec says (R4, R5). The asset change is limited to material parameters in build_patch_one.py. Silicone grain scale goes from 8 to 2 and normal strength from .65 to .85. LED emission goes from .5 to 1.4. Trace contact material becomes a metallic copper-gold. The client adds a PMREM studio environment, rebalanced lights, exposure .95, and per-material envMapIntensity, lens and silicone adjustments. Stack order, translations, layer thicknesses, footprint, wordmark and LED geometry are untouched, since only material nodes changed.; Asset budget: the builder reports the GLB at 798,088 bytes against the 819,200 limit, down 4 bytes from 798,092. The module and the Blender build logs (blender-build-1.log and blender-build-2.log) are committed for the reproducibility check. I did not re-run the Blender build.; Tests and capture script: SETUP_COMMIT is re-based to 62f98b3 in both test files, and take-apart.test.js's scope allowlist is rewritten to the S10 list. This fits the S10 allowance for scope or baseline constants re-based for this order, but the allowlist rewrite is larger than a one-constant change. The reviewer-tests station should confirm no assertion changed meaning. The capture script change is a small CAPTURE_DIR env override that leaves the default output paths unchanged. That is justified by the before/after requirement (R7), and the script still runs the bundled Worker, not the unbundled source.; Client structure: the on-load material handling stays inside the existing per-layer material clone, so material ownership per layer and the baseOpacity binding are preserved. Two fragile points, neither a blocker. The silicone onBeforeCompile patch string-replaces three.js shader chunk text ('normalScale;'), which only works while the vendored three.js bytes stay frozen as the spec requires. The source uses '\\n' escapes inside the GLSL strings. The after browser-pass.log records 0 console errors and 0 page errors with scene ready, so it works in the bundled output, but this is worth a note for any future three.js bump.; Evidence layout matches R7 and R8. Before/ and after/ each hold five beats, a contact sheet, a browser screenshot, a browser-pass.log and a bundle-build.log, and the after log shows zero errors. Whether the page rendering actually closes the shield, battery and sensor, silicone grain and LED problems is a visual judgement for reviewer-design. It is outside this architecture review, and I make no claim either way.; The builder reports the suite as green except the known S11 failure and one existing skip. I did not re-run the suite. Deployment stays out of the run, which is correct.; R3/S5 remains unmet: evidence/web-render-finish/after/beat-assembled.png and beat-mid.png show the LED as a muted gray-green stripe, without a clearly readable teal emitter separated from its recessed socket shadow. Compared with design/reference/product-reference.png, the optical identity remains washed out. Adjust client material/lighting handling while preserving geometry, then regenerate bundled evidence.; R2/S4 improved sufficiently: the after board beats show silver face highlights, darker packages, gold contacts and metallic sensor rims distinctly against the substrate. Fine cover grain is now visible in the assembled browser beat.; R6/S6: rounded-square silhouette, wordmark and five-layer order remain recognizable, accounting for the documented vertical exaggeration. Full identity clearance is withheld because the browser LED still fails the reference's teal-emitter read. The regenerated beauty cover also has substantially coarser grain than the fine silicone finish in quality-board-2.png; reduce that coarseness while retaining browser readability.

human_gate.rule: Verdict is changes_requested, not approved, so a human is required.
